newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bank stocks surging on strong profit outlook.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bank stocks surging on strong profit outlook.

text.p: Share prices of Switzerland's three big banks have risen sharply since early June as investors gradually look to position themselves for what promises to be a very strong first half performance in the sector.

With huge write-offs and provisions behind them and restructuring programmes in advanced stages or mostly completed, the banks are expected to report year-on-year first half profit increases of some 50 percent or better.

Zurich share traders said one factor was a recommendation by Morgan Stanley to switch to Swiss banks from German banks. Morgan Stanley on Monday issued a total of four million warrants on a basket of Swiss bank shares.
"It's the lower provisions, bourse volumes and (low) interest rates," said Bank Sarasin analyst Franco Catanzaro.
Swiss banks all suffered last year from high loan-loss provisions and credit losses in their domestic business as a result of the sharp and lasting downturn in the Swiss economy.
The big three -- Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), Credit Suisse Group and Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) -- all took massive extraordinary charges and as a result reported full-year losses.

Catanzaro has not yet completed his forecast for UBS, but he has recently predicted a 48 percent first half profit rise at CS to 1.23 billion francs ($840.7 million) and a 63.4 percent increase to 1.18 billion at Swiss Bank Corp.
"The banks may have achieved record results in this exceptional environment," Zuercher Kantonalbank (ZKB) said in its Daily Market Opinion comments on Tuesday.
ZKB predicted strong performances from all three banks but has picked Swiss Bank Corp as its favourite.
It upgraded CS Group to a buy from hold while downgrading UBS, which has undergone the most pronounced outperformance of the big three banks, to a hold from a buy.

It also said a favourable interest rates environment has led to enormous stock exchange turnover and the three business segments which contribute most to profit improvement -- commissions, service and trading -- account for some 76 percent of gross profits at CS.
The percentage was considerably higher than at the other two big banks in Switzerland. For example, the three segments accounted for some 62 percent of gross profits at UBS, ZKB said.
"Under the forementioned optimal conditions fantastic half-year are to be expected," the ZKB report said.
On the other hand, it said the UBS share price has risen by 51 percent since the end of January, outperforming the Swiss Performance Index by eight percent and CS Group by four percent.
It also said that in the difficult U.S. market, UBS has had only limited success in getting a foothold.

Catanzaro has not yet completed his forecast for UBS, but he has recently predicted a 48 percent first half profit rise at CS to 1.23 billion francs and a 63.4 percent increase to 1.18 billion at Swiss Bank Corp.
"The banks may have achieved record results in this exceptional environment," ZKB said in its report.
It also said that although interest income may remain around prior-year levels, service income probably rose by between 20 and 30 percent at the big banks and trading income by as much as 50 percent.
The share prices of the three banks have been rising steadily since the start of the year. They moved into a higher gear about a month ago.
CS which rose 6.25 to close at 203.50 on Monday, was up to another 4.75 to 208.25 in afternoon bourse trading for gain of nearly 25 francs since early June.
Swiss Bank Corp is at 428.50 as compared to 353 at the start of June and UBS has risen by more than 140 francs to 1,733. ($ = 1.463 Swiss Francs)
